item.title: [ 89] New Switch 2 model by Q4 2026
item.description:
https://www.gonintendo.com/contents/56723-rumor-nintendo-account-portal-discovery-leads-to-new-switch-2-model-speculation
>Being released as the Nintendo Switch 2 OLED.
>4NM chip, meaning better battery life (the original Switch 2 uses a 10NM chip with 8NM characteristics).
>6-10 hours of battery life.
>Supports DisplayPort 2.1, meaning the USB-C port on the console supports 80Gbs, meaning 4K at 120Hz support in TV mode.
>New dock is required as it uses the dual USB-C connector found on Switch 2 dev kits (left port is audio/video (through DisplayPort 2.1) and the right port is data (though USB 4.2, 80Gbs, top USB-C port as the same bandwidth).
>Dock is all USB-C, 3 ports, ethernet port is replaced with a 3rd USB-C port so if you have fast internet you're able to use a 10Gbs USB-C ethernet adaptor instead of being stuck with 1Gbs ethernet through a internal chipset.
>Removeable battery.
>No more removable Joy Cons due to lack of demand, new model of Joy Con 2s will have a analog trigger (ZL/ZR depending on the Joy Con 2 itself), TMR analog stick, USB-C connectivity and a removeable battery.
>Because the controls are no longer removeable a new model pro-controller will be bundled with the new Switch model that has analog triggers (COD coming back to Nintendo systems pushed them to include them, that and GameCube NSO), TMR analog sticks, 2 extra grip buttons (now having 4 of them), fast charging support and a removeable battery.
>Micro SD Express is replaced with a proper M.2 slot (supports up to 2280) as M.2 sticks are cheaper and easier to fund, plus the extra space of the new model allows for it.
>PSU is now at 100W (up from 60W), required for the new model.
>1TB of built in storage, up from 256GB.
>OLED screen.
>$600USD, parts are cheaper/easier to locate then the original, but the 1TB of storage brought the cost up.
Thoughts?

item.title: [ 32] Today, a guy who works shift work was bragging to me about making $29 an hour.
item.description:
Today, a guy who works shift work was bragging to me about making $29 an hour. He very proudly and arrogantly claimed that he was middle class.

I told him that $29 an hour isn’t really a middle class income on its own. He then mentioned that his wife also works and I said,”ohh so you need dual income.” I asked how much she made, and he said about $45,000.

I did the math and pointed out that his $29 per hour wage works out to roughly $60,000 a year before tax. Combined with his wife’s income, their household brings in about $105,000 a year before tax. After taxes, their take home pay is probably somewhere around $80,000 a year. (lol)

I told him that, based on those numbers, I wouldn’t consider them middle class. He seemed to think that making $29 an hour automatically put him solidly in the middle class, but when you actually look at the household income and take home pay, it’s a lot more modest than he was making it sound. ($80k a year total household income)

I also mentioned to him studies show every class thinks they are middle class.

https://nypost.com/2026/06/02/us-news/trumps-freedom-250-event-on-national-mall-sabotaged-by-vandals/

Vandals sabotaged generators at President Trump’s Freedom 250 event, according to a spokeswoman — and fuel leached into underground water tanks, contaminating them.

A generator fuel line set up for temporary lights for a May 17 event was cut, causing fuel to seep into underground cisterns that collect rainwater under the Washington, DC, landmark, Freedom 250 spokeswoman Rachel Reisner told NBC News.

“Following the Freedom 250 team’s installation of temporary lighting on the National Mall, our equipment has been repeatedly targeted by vandals. The recent fuel leak was the direct result of that tampering,” she said.

“Upon discovering damage to a generator fuel line, Freedom 250 and our vendors mobilized within minutes, coordinated an immediate cleanup response, and fully remediated the site in close partnership with the National Park Service,” Reisner went on.

“We take our responsibility as stewards of the National Mall seriously and are working closely with the appropriate law enforcement authorities regarding these acts of vandalism.”

item.title: [ 49] Murdered Student Henry Nowak Camera Footage Released
item.description:
> Police cam footage: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GlDmsdYjbtg

https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crlpyw05l75o

Student Henry Nowak repeatedly told police officers "I can't breathe" as he lay dying in handcuffs after being stabbed, bodycam footage shows.

The 18-year-old Southampton student was handcuffed after killer Vickrum Digwa, 23, lied to police at the scene of the 2025 stabbing, claiming he had been the victim of a racist attack.

Footage released by the force, with permission from Nowak's family, shows him pleading "I've been stabbed" and an officer replying "I don't think you have mate".

Nowak suffered stab wounds to his legs and a fatal wound to his heart from a 21cm (8in) blade that Digwa said he carried as part of his Sikh faith. He was jailed for life with a minimum 21-year term.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said an investigation into the police force's actions was ongoing.

Speaking in the House of Commons earlier, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood revealed a police officer unrelated to the case had been misidentified and forced to relocate in order to protect him and his family.

The attorney general's office is also considering the jail sentence given to Digwa after receiving "multiple requests" to review it under the unduly lenient sentence (ULS) scheme.

Nowak's family, from Chafford Hundred, Essex, called his treatment by police "inhumane and degrading" and the force has apologised.

His father, Mark, said: "Henry told officers that he could not breathe nine times. He told them that he had been stabbed four times. Henry was pulled across the gravel, his hands forced behind his back and he was placed in handcuffs."

He said the contrast between how his son and Digwa had been treated was "unbearable".

"Henry should not have died on the streets of Southampton in police custody," he added.
